children: Taiwan has stepped up measures to stabilise its stock market as a global sell-off in artificial intelligence-linked shares intensifies, with the benchmark TAIEX suffering its steepest weekly decline in more than three decades.

The Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) has introduced fresh restrictions on short selling, including a blanket ban on short sales at prices below the previous day's closing level. It has also raised the minimum margin requirement for short selling to 150% from 130%, while temporarily suspending applications from securities firms to list new put warrants.
The restrictions apply to both margin short sales and borrowed shares. However, short sales undertaken by securities and futures firms for hedging purposes will be exempt.

This marks the third time Taiwan has introduced additional short-selling curbs in November as authorities seek to contain the sharp decline in equities amid concerns over the unwinding of the global AI trade.
The National Financial Stabilization Fund has also entered the market to support share prices, although the measures have so far done little to reverse the broader sell-off.
Taiwan stocks suffer worst week since 1991
The TAIEX plunged 6.2% on Friday, taking its losses for the week to 18%. This marked its worst weekly performance since 1991, as investors pulled back from technology and AI-linked stocks.
The correction has also erased a significant portion of the index's gains. The TAIEX is now down 27% from its 52-week high, while its gains for the year have narrowed to around 24%.
Global funds have sold more than $56 billion worth of Taiwanese stocks so far this quarter, according to Bloomberg data, adding to the pressure on the market.
The selling has been compounded by forced liquidations among retail investors, as leveraged positions came under pressure following the steep decline in share prices.
Why is forced selling adding to the pressure?

Barclays has flagged the role of retail margin financing in amplifying the market correction. According to the brokerage, stocks that declined 7% or more had aggregate margin financing ratios 4.6 times higher than those of better-performing shares.

While margin financing across the broader market accounts for only around 0.38% of total market capitalisation, the risks are more concentrated in individual stocks, particularly those linked to the AI trade.

As share prices fall, investors holding leveraged positions may be forced to sell holdings to meet margin requirements. Such liquidations can add to downward pressure, triggering further declines and additional selling.
Barclays cautioned that the forced selling by retail investors could continue to weigh on Taiwanese equities.

The pressure has been particularly pronounced in AI-linked stocks, where elevated valuations and leveraged retail positions have left some investors more vulnerable to sharp price swings. Barclays noted that the market-wide margin financing ratio may appear relatively low, but the concentration of borrowing in individual stocks has made the impact of forced liquidations more severe.

The latest short-selling restrictions and intervention by the stabilisation fund have provided only limited relief so far, suggesting that authorities are still struggling to contain the market's downward momentum.
What next for Taiwan's stock market?
The near-term outlook remains challenging, with Barclays warning that retail investors' forced selling could continue to weigh on the market as leveraged positions are unwound.

The National Financial Stabilization Fund has been buying shares since November 6 to support the market. The fund has indicated that selling by foreign institutional investors has gradually eased, although the scale of the recent outflows has intensified concerns about the sustainability of the recovery.

With the TAIEX still around 27% below its 52-week high, investors will be watching whether the latest restrictions and state-backed buying can restore confidence or whether continued liquidation of leveraged positions triggers further volatility.

title: Global AI Sell-off: Taiwan takes action yet again to support collapsing stock market
